Starting from a pure product state, we analytically determine the time evolution of entanglement entropy, antiflatness, capacity of entanglement, and nonlocal trace distance magic under unitary dynamics generated by random matrix Hamiltonians drawn from all three Gaussian ensembles. We find that the transient maxima of antiflatness, capacity of entanglement, and nonlocal magic occur on the same characteristic timescale as the maximum rate of entanglement growth. These results establish that the magic barrier is a universal feature of RMT thermalization, suggesting universality across quantum chaotic systems. We conclude that quantitative simulations of thermalization in ergodic quantum theories inherently require quantum computation.

title: Quantum Cosmology in Page-Wootters' Framework: Singularity Resolution and Clock Coherence
summary: We investigate the fate of big-bang singularity and coherence between distinct clock states in a quantum cosmological setting within the Page-Wootters framework. With a canonically quantized plane-symmetric Bianchi I universe, we employ Dirac factorization of the Wheeler-DeWitt constraint and obtain a Schrodinger-like equation which is first-order in an internal clock variable. By constructing its solution as a Gaussian wave packet in the expanding branch, we derive the corresponding conditional state and probability density of the universe. We find that the conditional probability density vanishes in the zero-volume limit, indicating resolution of the big-bang singularity within this probabilistic framework. Another prespective of the study is provided by the construction of density matrix from the conditional states associated with different clock readings and the remaining degree of freedom. By tracing out the remaining subsystem, we obtain the reduced density matrix and analyze the resulting coherence as a function of separation between different clock states. These results provide a relational characterization of singularity resolution and demonstrate how the spectral properties of the quantum state govern the temporal coherence between different clock states in the Page-Wootters description.

title: An Attenuation Bump at z=9.3: Probing Dust Diversity at Cosmic Dawn
comment: paper submitted to ApJ, Figure 8 summarizes the key finding of this work
summary: We report the identification of a UV attenuation bump in the Black Pearl, a galaxy at a spectroscopic redshift of 9.3335 observed with JWST/NIRSpec as part of the ZENITH and EMBER surveys. This is the highest-redshift UV bump reported to date, probing dust properties only approximately 500 Myr after the Big Bang. The feature is directly detected as a broad depression in the rest-frame UV continuum and is well described by a local Drude profile, with a central wavelength of 2132+/-17 Angstroms, an FWHM of 413+/-54 Angstroms, and a peak attenuation of 0.21+/-0.02 mag. Joint spectrophotometric modeling with a flexible attenuation law independently recovers a pronounced UV bump without imposing its presence a priori, regardless of the adopted star-formation history. The modeling indicates a relatively low-mass, actively star-forming galaxy, with a logarithmic stellar mass of 8.35 (+0.09/-0.08) in solar units, a star-formation rate of 2.36 (+0.54/-0.42) solar masses per year, and a visual attenuation of 0.34 (+0.12/-0.11) mag. Rest-frame optical emission-line diagnostics indicate a hard ionizing spectrum and allow for a moderate AGN contribution, but provide no evidence for a powerful AGN capable of dominating the observed UV continuum. The bump is blueshifted by 43+/-17 Angstroms (approximately 2.5 sigma) relative to the canonical Milky Way 2175 Angstrom feature and by 127 +/- 17 Angstroms relative to the few UV bumps currently known at redshift approximately 7, while its width is consistent with the broad distribution measured along Milky Way sightlines. The displaced central wavelength therefore provides the clearest evidence for a nonstandard UV-bump profile at redshift 9.3335, pointing to substantial diversity in the properties of UV-bump carriers at early cosmic times, with both PAHs and small graphite grains remaining plausible candidates.

title: Modal estimation of high-order wavefront drifts on coronagraphic testbeds for high-contrast direct imaging of exoplanets
summary: Long-term wavefront stability will be critical for the upcoming Habitable Worlds Observatory which aims to directly image exo-Earths. Mechanical and thermal instabilities induce slow, high-order wavefront errors which can degrade the contrast and in turn, the scientific yield of the observatory. Dark zone maintenance (DZM) has been proposed as a high-order wavefront sensing and control strategy to maintain contrast despite wavefront error drifts. This approach uses an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) to estimate the electric field at each pixel in the dark zone of the science camera. However, relying on individual pixel information to estimate wavefront errors can discard information stored in the underlying wavefront. This is a fundamental limitation on the best achieved contrast compared to the model based theoretical bounds derived from photon noise. An alternative EKF can incorporate more holistic information by estimating the drifting wavefront modes present in the system. In this work we analyze the performance of this Modal EKF on the High-contrast Imager for Complex Aperture Telescopes (HiCAT) simulator at the Space Telescope Science Institute. A parameter scan is performed across key variables: deformable mirror (DM) drift, the direct photon rate at the telescope aperture governing the mean number of photons in the dark zone (DZ), and the dither magnitude used to provide phase diversity. While prior studies explored a range of dither magnitudes, this work introduces a covariance-based approach within the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) framework to optimally determine the probe magnitude required. Results from the modal EKF demonstrate a 15-fold improvement in contrast relative to the single-pixel DZM experiments, reducing the gap to within a factor of 2-3 of the theoretical bounds.

title: Bounds on hadronic contributions to the anomalous magnetic moment of the $τ$ lepton from QCD Sum Rules
summary: A QCD sum-rule study is performed to place bounds on the leading-order (LO) hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the $τ$ lepton ($a_τ^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO},\, a_τ= (g-2)_τ/2$). The QCD contributions to $a_τ^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO}$ are modeled as a combination of Laplace QCD sum rules (LSRs) and finite-energy QCD sum rules (FESRs) of various weights, which are bounded by Hölder and related fundamental inequalities. The light-quark ($u,\,d,\,s$) contributions are evaluated up to five-loop order in perturbative contributions in the chiral limit, LO in light quark mass corrections, next-to-leading order (NLO) in dimension-four QCD condensates and to LO in dimension-six QCD condensates. Extending previous work on $a_μ^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO}$, we present a robust methodology for using QCD sum rules to constrain $a_τ^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO}$, and more generally any lepton $g-2$. A criterion is developed to extract from the bounds analysis a final result of $a_τ^\mathrm{QCD} = \left( 3.385\pm 0.048 \right) \times 10^{-6}$, which after inclusion of charmonium and bottomonium contributions gives a final result $a_τ^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO} = \left( 3.501\pm0.048\right) \times 10^{-6}$, comparable to data-driven and lattice predictions. Lattice QCD results along with our value for $a_τ^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO}$ are used to obtain a combined QCD determination from lattice and sum-rule methods of $a_μ^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO} = (7.217\pm0.233)\times10^{-8}$. Our analysis provides fundamental QCD sum-rule inputs into the theoretical determinations of $a_τ$, and establishes new methodologies for QCD sum-rule determinations of low-energy observables.

title: The gravitational constant and the cosmic microwave background
summary: The CMB constrains the gravitational constant $G$ at recombination to a few percent of its laboratory value, but the effect of $G$ on recombination itself is usually absorbed into a global fit rather than made explicit. We return to the semi-analytic description of the acoustic spectrum to ask how the acoustic scale $\ell_A$, the equality scale $\ell_{\rm eq}$ and the damping scale $\ell_{\rm damp}$ respond to a variation of $G$ during recombination, and where $G$ enters the residual ionization of the dark ages. We use a modified version of CLASS in which $G$ is varied through $λ_G \equiv \sqrt{G/G_{\rm N}}$, scanning $λ_G \in [0.25,2]$ at fixed physical densities and CMB temperature, with helium recomputed for each model. Analytic rate arguments are confronted with the numerical ionization histories, the visibility function, the Hu & White damping integral and the TT spectra. While $\ell_{\rm eq}$ and $\ell_A$ are nearly independent of $G$, non-equilibrium recombination gives $\ell_{\rm damp} \propto λ_G^{-0.304}$. The dependence exists only above a critical value of $G$, set by fundamental and cosmological parameters, a factor of 49 below $G_{\rm N}$. The dark-ages optical depth varies by only 16% for $G$ multiplied by 64, a negligible channel. Because $G$ enters only through the expansion rate, the imprint comes entirely from out-of-equilibrium recombination, and the competition between the atomic rates and the expansion is governed by one dimensionless combination, $α_G \equiv G m_e μ/\hbar c$, with $μ$ the mean mass of matter per photon. Each scale is the distance to last scattering divided by a length imprinted before it, so a late-time change of gravity rescales all three alike. The ratio $\ell_{\rm damp}/\ell_A$ therefore isolates $G$ at recombination and, up to lensing and screening, compares it directly with the laboratory value.

title: All Order Gravitational Wave Tails for Subleading Post-Newtonian Expansion
summary: The low-frequency gravitational waveform emitted in a classical scattering process contains an infinite tower of late- and early-time tail terms of the form $u^{-r}(\ln|u|)^{r-1}$, $r \geq 1$. In the Newtonian limit, the coefficients of this entire tower have recently been shown to be universal, i.e. fixed by the asymptotic data of the scattering objects alone. At the retained order in the velocity expansion, these leading-logarithmic tails are determined to all orders in Newton's constant $G$. We extend this result to the first subleading order in the post-Newtonian expansion of the asymptotic states. We consider scattering of an arbitrary number of incoming and outgoing nonrelativistic objects interacting only through gravity at long range, and we derive the complete tower of tail terms at this order. The correction arises from the first subleading term in the retardation expansion and is determined by the asymptotic Newtonian trajectories of the massive particles. Its coefficients are again determined entirely by the asymptotic trajectories and are independent of the details of the interaction. For $2\to2$ scattering, the leading-logarithmic series can be summed in closed form. Our results agree with a relativistic conjecture proposed in earlier work arXiv:2610.07134.

title: Numerical simulations of low-mass black hole-neutron star mergers with moderate eccentricities
comment: 24 pages, 8 figures, to be submitted to PRD
summary: A confident detection of orbital eccentricity in gravitational-wave signals from black hole-neutron star systems would be a strong indicator of their dynamical formation origin. While eccentric waveform models have recently been developed, their validity for analyzing black hole--neutron star signals has yet to be tested against numerical-relativity simulations. Building upon our previous study of quasicircular black hole--neutron star mergers, we perform simulations of a subset of these systems with orbital eccentricities around five times larger than those inferred for GW200105_162426. Additionally, we perform simulations with magnetized matter to assess whether trapped $g$-mode oscillations persist in strongly magnetized disks. Regarding the emitted gravitational-wave signal, we find that the effective one-body waveform model SEOBNRv5EHM shows reasonable agreement unless tidal contributions become important, and the inspiral-only post-Newtonian models pyEFPE/pyEFPEHM show larger disagreement in the late inspiral. For the equal-mass system, which has the largest effective tidal deformability, eccentric tidal corrections have a small but noticeable impact on the phase, $\sim0.1$ rad. We find an almost negligible impact of eccentricity on the properties of the remnant black hole, and differences of up to a factor of two in the remnant disk mass. Trapped $g$ modes in the accretion disks have the same frequency regardless of the eccentricity, confirming that they depend mainly on the properties of the remnant black hole. We find that when accretion disks are strongly magnetized, they become less dense and have less pronounced structure, and that the trapped $g$ modes previously identified in the unmagnetized cases are efficiently damped.

title: A model for the ongoing subcluster interaction in Centaurus
comment: Submitted to Astronomy and Astrophysics; comments welcome
summary: Intracluster globular clusters (GCs) preserve the hierarchical and chemical history of galaxy cluster assembly. The nearby Centaurus cluster is believed to be undergoing an interaction between two subclusters, Cen 30 and Cen 45, which should leave an imprint on its intracluster GCs. We aim to characterise the GC population in Centaurus and constrain its recent assembly history, ultimately constructing an interaction scenario consistent with the observational evidence. Using deep VLT/FORS imaging in the $V$ and $I$ bands, we select GC candidates around the cluster centre based on morphology and colour criteria. We use a Voronoi tessellation approach to study the GC spatial distribution and density profiles, demonstrating its advantages over traditional annuli-based methods. We then constrain the evolution of the galaxy luminosity function using the GC specific frequency and colour distribution. The GC spatial distribution shows significant substructure. As in other clusters, red GCs are concentrated on the brightest galaxies, whereas blue GCs trace a more extended structure. We confirm and quantify the previously reported 'bridge' of GCs connecting NGC 4696 and NGC 4709, showing that it hosts twice as many GCs as expected from the projected GC systems of the two galaxies alone. The inferred evolution of the galaxy luminosity function agrees with previous results for Hydra I, yielding a faint-end slope of $α=-1.87_{-0.06}^{+0.06}$ for the galaxy population that assembled the Centaurus core. We propose a nearly head-on collision scenario in which Cen 45 recently passed through Cen 30, with the two subclusters moving approximately along the line of sight. This scenario explains the large line-of-sight velocity difference between the subclusters, the hot X-ray-emitting gas between them, the GC bridge, and the puffed-up GC system of NGC 4709.

title: Correlated Radio Frequency Interference Monitor for Radio Telescopes
summary: Radio frequency interference (RFI) is one of the biggest challenges facing current radio astronomy experiments. Telescopes like the Canadian Hydrogen Observatory and Radio transient Detector (CHORD) need to accurately identify RFI to deliver on their science goals. For applications like HI intensity mapping for precision cosmology, long integrations consisting of hundreds to thousands of hours are needed, and thorough RFI flagging is required to avoid contaminating deep datasets. Currently, many major precision cosmology instruments are facing systematic limitations that include unflagged RFI contamination. For transients, false triggers due to RFI are common and interfere with the detection of real sources like fast radio bursts (FRBs). This paper presents a prototype design for an auxiliary array of horizon-pointed antennas that are cross-correlated in real-time at full cadence with the main telescope to assist in the identification and mitigation of RFI for the CHORD instrument. The major benefit of the version proposed here over a more traditional omnidirectional observatory monitor is the capability to synchronize with CHORD in real time and provide fine timescale flags and cross correlations. The general setup and techniques used here will be applicable to other radio telescopes as well.

title: The Sill distribution for all partial waves
summary: In high-energy physics, short-lived resonances appearing in scattering processes are described by energy-dependent spectral functions. The relativistic Breit--Wigner distribution (rBW), obtained as a relativistic extension of the standard Breit--Wigner form, is commonly employed owing to its simplicity. However, when the lower-energy threshold lies sufficiently close to the resonance peak, sizable deviations from the rBW line shape are expected. The Sill distribution provides a simple way to incorporate the physical threshold while preserving exact normalization, but in its original formulation it is inherently restricted to $s$-wave decays. Here, we extend the Sill distribution to arbitrary partial waves. The correct $\ell$-wave threshold behaviour is implemented while exact normalization is retained through a simple modification of the mass term of the propagator. As a benchmark, the $p$-wave Sill provides a very good description of the $Δ(1232)^{++}$ line shape up to 1.35 GeV and simultaneously reproduces its on-shell mass and width and its complex pole position, in agreement with independent determinations compiled by the PDG.

title: Breaking de Sitter Symmetry with Cosmic Topology: Cosmological Role of Infrared Vacuum Freedom
summary: When spatial sections of spacetime are topologically nontrivial, the symmetry arguments usually used to choose the Bunch-Davies vacuum are no longer guaranteed to apply. We study this problem for a scalar field on de Sitter spacetime with toroidal spatial sections. The Hadamard conditions, which ensure the same short-distance structure as in flat space, are local and naturally insensitive to the compactification. By contrast, we find that the infrared sector is affected by the toroidal identifications that break global de Sitter invariance, thereby removing the usual argument for discarding zero-mode contributions. We treat the remaining zero-mode freedom as an effective topology-induced source and analyze its effects on an inflationary de Sitter expansion within a semiclassical setting. We show that, for a massless scalar, the zero-mode sector can contain a contribution to the stress-energy tensor with equation of state $P=-ρ$, behaving as a cosmological constant. Thus, the source driving an early-Universe de Sitter phase need not be determined solely by local terms in the action, but can also depend on the infrared structure of the quantum state. Nontrivial topology, as a concrete realization of de Sitter symmetry violation, turns the otherwise-unfixed infrared freedom in vacuum selection to a contribution directly relevant to the semiclassical expansion. This contribution could potentially be applicable to the current accelerated expansion of the Universe.

title: Exact AdS and pp-waves in multi-gravity beyond pairwise interactions
summary: We construct exact anti-de Sitter (AdS) waves and pp-waves in ghost-free multi-gravity beyond pairwise interactions for an arbitrary number $\mathcal{N}$ of vielbeins, in any spacetime dimension $D\geq3$. Deforming proportional AdS and Minkowski solutions along a common null direction reduces the full nonlinear field equations to coupled linear differential equations for the wave profiles, without restricting their amplitudes. The system is diagonalised in the same eigenbasis as the perturbative Fierz-Pauli mass matrix, separating the solutions into one massless and $\mathcal{N}-1$ massive eigenprofiles. We obtain explicit radial and transverse solutions and impose an AdS boundary falloff. This falloff admits the appropriate radial branch of every mode with non-negative squared mass and excludes profiles with negative squared masses, including logarithmic solutions at the Breitenlohner-Freedman threshold. We also relate the AdS waves to pp-waves through a local flat limit. Explicit examples exhibit wave configurations that cannot be reproduced by ghost-free pairwise theories, demonstrating that genuine multi-field interactions support new exact gravitational-wave solutions.

title: From Cosmic Bounces to Primordial Black Holes: The Role of Primordial Magnetic Fields
summary: We investigate primordial black hole (PBH) formation from primordial magnetic fields generated during a non-singular ekpyrotic bounce. A time-dependent coupling between the electromagnetic field and a scalar background breaks conformal invariance and amplifies gauge field fluctuations during contraction, generating magnetic fields whose anisotropic stress dominates during radiation domination. By retaining finite-wavenumber cutoffs, we compute the ultraviolet-dominated curvature spectrum, evaluate density-perturbation variance, and determine PBH abundances using both monochromatic and critical-collapse prescriptions. For benchmark parameters, the critical collapse mass spectrum peaks at $M\simeq 2.0\times10^{-3}M_\odot$ , with a total PBH dark matter fraction of $f_{PBH}\approx 10^{-5}$, forming a subdominant subsolar PBH population. Enforcing the cosmological overclosure bound ($f_{\mathrm{PBH}} \le 1$) constrains the primary background parameters, namely the end-of-contraction Hubble scale ($H_{\mathrm{end}} \le 1.6 \times 10^3~\mathrm{GeV}$) and the contraction exponent ($q \le 0.247$), establishing a physical boundary consistent with the electromagnetic backreaction limit. Shifting to asteroid-mass PBHs or a larger dark matter fraction requires modifying the ultraviolet cutoff and contraction duration. This analysis highlights the essential role of finite-wavenumber cutoffs and assumed-collapse prescriptions in linking bounce magnetogenesis to the predicted PBH abundance.

title: The ALMA-QUARKS Survey. IV. Core Mass Function and Evolutionary Trends in Core Formation Efficiency and Chemistry
comment: 28 pages, 14 figures, submitted to the ApJS
summary: The ALMA-QUARKS (Querying Underlying Mechanisms of Massive Star Formation with ALMA-Resolved Gas Kinematics and Structures) survey targets 139 massive protoclusters selected from the ATOMS survey. The targets were observed at 1.3~mm wavelength with an angular resolution of $\sim0.3^{\prime\prime}$, corresponding to $\sim10^3$~au at the sample's median distance of $\sim3.8$~kpc. Using \texttt{getsf}, we identify 3374 dense cores and classify them as starless, protostellar, hot core, or H{\sc ii} region candidates based on spectral-line diagnostics (e.g., H30$α$, CH$_3$CN, and CH$_3$OH) and CO outflow associations. The resulting catalog provides core physical properties and enables statistical investigations of dense core populations in massive protocluster environments. The derived global core mass function (CMF) after excluding H{\sc ii} region candidates, which is biased by distance effects, has a relatively flat power-law slope at the high-mass end ($\mathrm{d}N/\mathrm{d}\log M \propto M^{-γ}$, with $γ=0.98\pm0.03$). In contrast, the measured high-mass slopes in individual distance bins are approximately Salpeter-like, while their fitted lower mass limits increase with distance. We further examine the core formation efficiency (CFE) across the full sample and find that it positively correlates with the luminosity-to-mass ratio of the parental clumps, consistent with an evolutionary increase in the fraction of mass concentrated into dense cores. We also investigate the detection rates of different molecular tracers and find systematic chemical variations with evolutionary stage. Compared with the ASHES survey, we find that the detection rates of deuterated species vary significantly even for cores at the same evolutionary stages, suggesting an important environmental influence on the chemical evolution of cores.

title: Unveiling the Baryon Cycle Through Cosmic Time
comment: Part of the ALMA2040 White Paper Series. 11 pages, 4 figures, 1 table
summary:
Galaxy evolution is governed by the baryon cycle: gas accreted from the cosmic web and circumgalactic medium condenses into molecular gas, forms stars, and is redistributed by stellar and AGN feedback. Tracing the molecular phase is therefore essential to understanding how galaxies acquire, consume, and eject their baryons. Yet current molecular-gas surveys remain limited by sensitivity, area, cosmic variance, and spectral bandwidth.
  ALMA2040 would combine a $\sim10\times$ sensitivity improvement with $\gtrsim512$ GHz simultaneous frequency coverage, delivering $\sim100\times$ faster mapping at fixed depth and a further $\gtrsim25\times$ gain in instantaneous bandwidth. Together, these advances would increase spectroscopic survey speed by orders of magnitude, enabling tiered ``wedding-cake'' strategies: an ultra-deep $\sim4$-5 arcmin$^2$ field probing faint and high-redshift reservoirs, a $\sim$0.25 deg$^2$ survey reaching molecular-line sensitivities comparable to current ultra-deep fields over a much larger cosmological volume, and thousands of independent pointings minimizing cosmic variance.
  Broad spectral coverage would simultaneously detect multiple CO transitions, [CI], H$_2$O, feedback tracers, far-IR fine-structure lines, and dust continuum, constraining molecular gas, ISM conditions, obscured star formation, and gas flows within the same observations. Every targeted observation would also become a molecular deep field, extending these measurements to serendipitous galaxies. Together with future HI, optical, and near-IR surveys, ALMA2040 would enable a population-resolved view of the baryon cycle across cosmic time and stringent tests of galaxy formation models.

title: Testing the inelastic dark matter interpretation of the LZ event with heavy-element experiments
summary: We consider the inelastic dark matter interpretation of the recent 248 keV event observed by LZ and identify different experiments that could test it. Details of the underlying model and the ability of complementary experiments to test it depend significantly on the high-velocity tail of the dark matter distribution. We consider several example velocity distributions motivated by the impact of the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) in order to map out the effects of this dependence. For example, we illustrate the type of high-velocity tail that would make the thermal Higgsino viable despite stringent constraints from solar neutrinos: Reducing the flux of the tail relative to simulation results improves the Higgsino fit, while extending the tail to higher velocities at fluxes below current simulation resolution evades the solar neutrino bound. This motivates more detailed simulations at higher resolution to understand the tail better. Even if xenon experiments confirm the signal event, complementary experiments are still required to test whether the underlying model is inelastic dark matter and to break degeneracies in the measurement of dark matter parameters such as mass and mass splitting. Heavy-element paleodetectors could cover most of the parameter space relevant to the LZ event. Their use of different elements could determine the dark matter mass and splitting, while their unique sensitivity to the history of the dark matter distribution could test the signal's LMC origin. Luminous detection in large neutrino detectors with heavy-element supplements could directly test the inelastic nature of the signal and measure the mass splitting, while its sensitivity to the radiative decay rate could provide strong evidence for the Higgsino interpretation.

title: The Forgetful Black Hole: Memory Burden and Hysteresis in Hawking Evaporation
summary: The memory-burden scenario of black hole evaporation proposes that Hawking emission may become increasingly suppressed as maintaining stored quantum information becomes dynamically costly. In this work, we revisit this scenario and investigate the conditions under which information retention can produce a genuine dynamical burden. We derive general scaling conditions for incremental memory accumulation at a fixed fractional mass loss and establish a conditional no-go result: entropy-suppressed, zero-mean deposits with subextensive integrated correlations cannot produce an order-one luminosity modification through unamplified accumulation and bounded feedback. We identify three essential requirements for dynamical memory: a record of the past must be written, retained, and coupled back to subsequent evaporation. We illustrate these requirements with concrete toy models that exhibit either a prolonged but finite black hole lifetime or an asymptotically approached finite-mass state (an effective remnant). We further distinguish kinetic-memory, thermodynamic-memory, and spectral-memory sub-categories of possible memory-burden mechanisms. In particular, we demonstrate that an independently evolving memory variable can generate evaporation-accretion hysteresis, such that a black hole returning to the same mass may possess a different retained memory and consequently a different luminosity. This history dependence may have implications for primordial black hole phenomenology. Finally, we briefly discuss the possibility of "merger rejuvenation", in which black hole mergers reorganize or reset the effective memory state.

title: Beyond the polynomial ansatz: regular $AdS_3\times M_8$ solutions of M-theory
summary: We study regular compact solutions of the cohomogeneity-one $AdS_3\times M_8$ system of Gauntlett, Mac Conamhna, Mateos and Waldram, where $M_8$ is an $S^2$ bundle over three constant-curvature Riemann surfaces. We find that an endpoint argument rules out every non-flat curvature-sign sector without a positive-curvature factor, while an analytic deformation gives regular families with four radial shape parameters in all remaining sectors, with the base geometry held fixed. The known polynomial solutions form a proper analytic locus in these families. Non-polynomiality is therefore generic in parameter space, although the deviation from an endpoint-matching polynomial can be very small. Apart from the completely flat exception, the curvature-sign criterion is necessary and sufficient within this ansatz. Four magnetic flux ratios give local coordinates near the reference solution and its small-curvature deformations, and a rational inverse reconstructs candidate endpoint data directly from finite flux ratios. In the fully positive sector we prove that one explicit four-dimensional finite-ratio neighbourhood lies inside the physical flux image. The magnetic periods and leading holographic central charge reduce to endpoint data, and, once the common Brown--Henneaux normalization is fixed, the nontrivial flux dependence of the equivariant localization formula agrees with the endpoint result as an exact algebraic identity. We also quantify the non-polynomial corrections and analyse finite degenerations under explicit convergence hypotheses.

title: An exact Simpson-Visser family in bumblebee gravity
comment: 56 pages, 22 figures and 7 tables. Suggestions (about the contents and refs) are welcome
summary: We construct an exact Simpson-Visser solution in metric bumblebee gravity, supported by a phantom scalar, magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics, and a spacelike configuration of fixed norm. The independent vector equation determines a local Lagrange multiplier and a temporal component that permits a regular ingoing extension across metric horizons. Reconstruction of the matter functions identifies a continuous family of wormholes, null minimum geometries, and black-bounces within one action. In the black hole case, the areal photon sphere and critical timelike orbit radii retain their Schwarzschild values, whereas angular deflection, periapsis advance, and photon orbit instability depend on the bounce and bumblebee parameters. The metric shadow coincides with the Schwarzschild prediction at fixed lapse mass and areal observer position; in addition, the adopted Sgr A* shadow diameter and M87* angular mass comparisons do not determine these parameters separately. The coupled axial equations yield distinct tensor, metric, and transverse bumblebee characteristics. We compute fundamental auxiliary massless scalar and ordinary Maxwell probe resonances by Chebyshev spectral collocation and estimate the tensor and bumblebee resonance scales at leading geometric optics order. Nonnegative probe potentials exclude exponentially growing probe modes. For negative nonminimal coupling and a nonzero temporal case, however, the supporting electromagnetic field develops an angular gradient instability in its extraordinary polarization. The unstable characteristic persists in the coupled principal symbol, while a variational construction establishes growing modes on the fixed geometry and lower bounds on their growth rates.

title: The optical colors of hidden spiral-like features in nine Virgo early--type dwarfs
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary: Dwarf early-type galaxies (ETGs) are abundant in nearby clusters and provide a key laboratory for studying environmentally driven galaxy transformation. Although dwarf ETGs were once considered structurally simple, deep imaging has revealed embedded spiral-like features (e.g., bars and spiral arms) in some of them, contributing only a small fraction of the total light. Their origin at dwarf scales remains uncertain. As a pilot study, we investigate spiral-like features in nine Virgo dwarf ETGs with clear embedded arms, using optical colors to test whether these features differ from the surrounding diffuse component, which would constrain their formation pathways. Using deep g- and i-band NGVS images, we apply a residual-based method to separate excess light associated with the spiral-like component from the diffuse host. The residual images define arm and interarm regions, enabling direct measurements of light fractions and g-i colors for both components. The spiral-like features contribute only a few percent of the total light (about 1.5-5.5% in i and 1.7-3.7% in g). We find a diverse range of colors across the sample: four galaxies host spiral-like features redder than their interarm regions, four show no robust arm-interarm color difference, and one exhibits a distinctly bluer spiral-like component. The latter is consistent with a recently quenched transition object, while the redder and color-uniform features are consistent with older or more metal-rich stellar populations. Spiral-like features in Virgo dwarf ETGs thus exhibit a surprising diversity in their photometric properties, implying multiple evolutionary channels rather than a single one. This pilot analysis also demonstrates readiness for the much larger NGVS sample of dwarfs with potential spiral-like features.

title: Optimization of multi-resolution observation strategies for cosmic microwave background experiments
summary: Cosmic microwave background (CMB) observations are increasingly performed by using a combination of both small aperture telescopes (SATs) and large aperture telescopes (LATs) to extract information across a wide variety of angular scales. The observation strategy of the telescopes must balance the restrictions of the observing site, instrument constraints, and a variety of science goals. We present a general framework for simulating the performance of different observation strategies. Using this framework, we focus primarily on the inflationary science goal and determine the optimal LAT coverage for delensing SAT measurements and present a novel deep scan strategy for an experiment in Chile that improves observation efficiency in the deepest 3% of the sky by 26%. Finally, we present considerations for future surveys to consider to further increase their observing efficiency.

title: Two-loop HTL-resummed thermodynamics for pure $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory
summary: We compute the two-loop hard-thermal-loop (HTL) resummed thermodynamic potential of pure four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory using regularization by dimensional reduction. Our result is gauge invariant and was renormalized using vacuum energy, gluon mass $m_d$ and quark mass $m_q$ counterterms. The thermal mass parameters are determined self-consistently and numerically from gap equations incorporating the running coupling. Based on these solutions, we numerically calculate the scaled pressure, entropy density, energy density, and trace anomaly and compare them with the results in the static perturbative limit through $\mathcal O(λ^2)$. For the first three quantities, next-to-leading-order (NLO) corrections are positive and have discernible effects at small coupling, and reduce the renormalization-scale dependence at relatively large couplings. We assess $m_q$-prescription dependence by comparing these results with those obtained by setting $m_q=0$. We find that it has a substantial impact on $m_d$ and the scalar mass $m_s$ at large couplings, and it reverses the signs of the NLO corrections to the first three quantities and qualitatively alters the trace anomaly.

title: Tracing small-scale structure formation through cosmic time with strong gravitational lensing: A case for a next-generation sub-millimetre/millimetre interferometer
comment: Part of the ALMA2040 White Paper Series
summary: The nature of dark matter and the growth of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) remain major open questions in modern astrophysics. Both leave a key signature in an overlapping, largely unexplored mass range: $<10^7$ M$_{\odot}$ dark haloes and wandering black holes. These may be undetectable directly, but detectable through gravitational perturbation of strongly lensed images, and partly or entirely distinguishable from one another through lensing data alone. We demonstrate through realistic simulations that a 255-element sub-mm/mm interferometer could probe this critical mass regime, detecting gravitational perturbations in strongly lensed dusty star-forming galaxies (DSFGs) from objects down to at least $10^5$ M$_{\odot}$. Combined with lens-galaxy characterisation from the European Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), which strengthens the physical interpretation of detected perturbers, and the unprecedented lens samples expected from Euclid and the Square Kilometre Array (SKA), this facility could deliver a census of low-mass dark matter haloes and wandering massive black holes across cosmic time.

title: Local supersymmetry implies momentum map/Gauntlett-Pakis equations and vanishing generalized Komar forms
summary: The first-order differential equations satisfied by Killing spinor bilinears (momentum map equations or Gauntlett--Pakis equations, Killing vector equations and the vanishing of the generalized Komar charge of the supersymmetric Killing vector) can be derived directly from the action of the local supersymmetry algebra on bosonic fields. We show how this comes about in several examples of increasing complexity, one of which is 11-dimensional supergravity.

title: Thermodynamics of rotating black holes with constrained primary hair
summary: An exact rotating geometry need not define a black hole in equilibrium when its surface gravity varies across the horizon. We construct an asymptotically flat, non-Kerr subfamily of the aligned null solutions of generalized Proca theory whose outer horizon is exactly Killing and isothermal to second order in rotation. The horizon conditions constrain the vector hair, and integrability of the normalized horizon charge fixes the remaining second-order amplitude. Computing the complete gravitational and nonminimal vector surface charges, we obtain the asymptotically normalized mass and total angular momentum, and derive a logarithmic Hamiltonian entropy. The first law holds in both independent directions of the resulting two-parameter solution space. We express the mass as a function of entropy and angular momentum, recover the geometric thermodynamic potentials, and establish a scale-corrected Smarr relation that retains the dimensionful coupling. The exact metric defines the geometry, while equilibrium thermodynamics is consistently restricted to second order in spin.

title: Self Calibrated Galaxy Groups from the DESI DR1 Bright Galaxy Survey
comment: 32 pages, 26 Figures, submitted to ApJ. See https://ianw89.github.io/catalogs.html or https://data.desi.lbl.gov/doc/releases/dr1/#value-added-catalogs to acquire the catalog
summary: We present a galaxy group catalog built from Data Release 1 of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Bright Galaxy Survey, using the Self Calibrated Group Finder. The algorithm uses clustering data from the observed sample to calibrate the Group Finder's free parameters, rather than simulations. The catalog contains 2,229,741 galaxies from ~$2680$ deg$^2$ of sky with 3-pass coverage and $r$-band fluxes $\lt 19.5$. The catalog classifies all galaxies in the flux-limited sample as centrals or satellites and estimates host dark matter halo masses. We show the satellite fraction $f_{\rm sat}$, luminosity halo mass relation, stellar halo mass relation and halo occupation distributions (HODs) from the catalog. We find these non-parametric HODs can be fit by standard HOD models, with satellite power-law index $α$ values around 0.75 for star-forming galaxies and around 1.1 for quiescent objects. In agreement with recent results, we find that the quenched fraction of central galaxies depends mostly on halo mass and is nearly independent of central galaxy stellar mass for galaxies more massive than $10^{10.3}$ $M_\odot h^{-1}$ and halos more massive than $10^{12.2}$ $M_\odot h^{-1}$. In an appendix, we introduce a new Hybrid Nearest Neighbor (HNN) technique to mitigate systematics from fiber incompleteness. HNN uses photometric redshifts and multiple on-sky neighbors to assign redshifts to unobserved targets. Calibrated on DESI Survey Validation 3 data, our technique yields correct redshifts $\sim 50\%$ of the time and produces unbiased halo occupation statistics.

title: The energetic atmosphere of the Sun
comment: Part of the ALMA2040 White Paper Series
summary: Understanding the mechanisms that heat the Sun's chromosphere and corona to temperatures far exceeding those of the solar photosphere below remains one of the central challenges in solar physics. Small-scale, rapidly evolving processes - including shocks, turbulence, magnetohydrodynamic waves, reconnection-driven jets, and nano-flares - are thought to contribute significantly to the heating budget. However, direct observational constraints on their spatial, temporal, and spectral signatures remain hard to obtain. At millimeter wavelengths, optically thick thermal emission provides a comparatively direct measure of gas temperature. While the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) already provides unique diagnostic capabilities, offering temperature diagnostics and high-cadence imaging, the current capabilities are still limiting the study of such dynamic, small-scale phenomena. Improved spatial resolution, enhanced uv-coverage, and simultaneous multi-band observations, as proposed for ALMA2040, would enable transformative progress in capturing dynamic processes across multiple heights and enable time-dependent three-dimensional thermal and magnetic tomography of the chromosphere. Combined with complementary diagnostics and simulations, these measurements would test how small-scale processes contribute to atmospheric heating.

title: PTagent: An LLM-assisted tool for finite-temperature model construction in cosmological phase transitions
summary: Cosmological phase-transition calculations require well-defined finite-temperature numerical models, whose construction involves assembling model information under consistent theoretical prescriptions. In this work we present \texttt{PTagent}, a large language model (LLM) agent-based framework for constructing such models from SARAH model files, research papers, and DRalgo sources. The LLM agent interprets and organizes model information and identifies unresolved physical choices, while dedicated backends perform the model-dependent calculations. After review and approval of the resulting physical model specification, the backends generate the corresponding CosmoTransitions-style or PhaseTracer-style numerical potentials. By separating model interpretation from numerical implementation, PTagent provides an inspectable and reproducible approach to finite-temperature model construction for cosmological phase-transition studies.

title: A model for the ongoing subcluster interaction in Centaurus
comment: Submitted to Astronomy and Astrophysics; comments welcome
summary: Intracluster globular clusters (GCs) preserve the hierarchical and chemical history of galaxy cluster assembly. We aim to characterise the GC population in Centaurus and constrain its recent assembly history, ultimately constructing an interaction scenario consistent with the observational evidence. Using deep VLT/FORS imaging in the $V$ and $I$ bands, we select GC candidates around the cluster centre based on morphology and colour criteria. We use a Voronoi tessellation approach to study the GC spatial distribution and density profiles, demonstrating its advantages over traditional annuli-based methods. We then constrain the evolution of the galaxy luminosity function using the GC specific frequency and colour distribution. The GC spatial distribution shows significant substructure. As in other clusters, red GCs are concentrated on the brightest galaxies, whereas blue GCs trace a more extended structure. We confirm and quantify the previously reported 'bridge' of GCs connecting NGC 4696 and NGC 4709, showing that it hosts twice as many GCs as expected from the projected GC systems of the two galaxies alone. The inferred evolution of the galaxy luminosity function agrees with previous results for Hydra I, yielding a faint-end slope of $α=-1.87_{-0.06}^{+0.06}$ for the galaxy population that assembled the Centaurus core. We propose a nearly head-on collision scenario in which Cen 45 recently passed through Cen 30, with the two subclusters moving approximately along the line of sight. This scenario explains the large line-of-sight velocity difference between the subclusters, the hot X-ray-emitting gas between them, the GC bridge, and the puffed-up GC system of NGC 4709.

title: Regge Dilaton Gravity from BF Theory
summary: In this work we investigate the relation between gauge and geometric descriptions of two-dimensional dilaton gravity at the level of discrete path integrals. We develop a Regge discretization of Euclidean two-dimensional dilaton gravity using homogeneously curved simplices, as well as a ribbon refined discretization of two-dimensional BF theory adapted to homogeneously curved spacetimes. For Euclidean signature and vanishing or negative cosmological constant we show how the ribbon BF discretization, through appropriate gauge fixings, leads to the Regge dilaton gravity formulation. The resulting correspondence makes explicit how a geometric Regge path integral with its associated measure emerges from its gauge theoretic formulation.

title: Photon-Return and Polar-Focusing Crossovers near Extremal Kerr
summary: How precisely must a photon's impact parameter be tuned for it to complete $n$ windings around a nearly extremal Kerr black hole before escaping, and how does the same near extremal scaling control the focusing of neighboring rays? For equatorial prograde returns we find, with $κ=\sqrt{1-a^2/M^2}$ and $X=nκ$, $ε_n=\sqrt{3}\,κ/(e^{2πX}-1) +O(κ^2|\lnκ|)$. This single law connects the extremal inverse-winding hierarchy to subextremal exponential accumulation. Perturbing the return family quasi-equatorially, we derive a second scaling law for the polar Jacobi phase, $Ψ_θ=2\ln[\sinh(πX)/κ]+C_s+o(1)$, and show that its focusing points cross from geometric spacing in winding number to asymptotically uniform spacing $Δ\mathcal N\simeq(2κ)^{-1}$. Numerical integrations of the exact Kerr radial dynamics and linear polar equation verify both scaling collapses. Thus near extremal Kerr exhibits parametrically distinct winding and polar-focusing scales, rather than a discontinuous jump between extremal and subextremal lensing hierarchies.

title: JWST reveals a highly ionized nebula powered by an ultraluminous X-ray source with a massive black hole in the metal-poor galaxy Holmberg II
summary: Recent James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations have revealed fine-structure lines of ions with ionization potentials ${\gtrsim}50$\,eV, such as [Ne\,{\sc v}] and [O\,{\sc iv}], in nebular spectra of some low-metallicity galaxies, raising questions about the nature of the ionizing sources. Ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) have been considered as potential contributors, but direct evidence linking individual ULXs to highly ionized nebulae is limited. Here we present JWST IFU spectroscopy of the nebula surrounding the template ULX Ho\,II\,X--1 in the low-metallicity galaxy Holmberg\,II, already known to emit He\,{\sc ii}\,$\lambda4686$ and [O\,{\sc iv}]\,25.89\,$μ$m lines. We resolve the infrared nebula on spatial scales of ${\sim}15-25$\,pc and report the first detections of [Ne\,{\sc v}] and [Ne\,{\sc vi}] in this source. We find anisotropic ionizing conditions: emission from the highest-ionization species arises from compact regions offset from the ULX toward the previously detected radio knots, whereas lower-ionization species trace the wider nebula. The preferential alignment of the highest-ionization emission with the radio axis suggests anisotropic escape of the ionizing continuum and a physical connection with jet-ejection activity. Spectral lines across the nebula are narrow and consistent with the instrumental resolution, indicating kinematically quiescent gas and disfavoring shocks as the dominant ionization mechanism. Together, these results provide direct evidence linking an individual ULX to a highly ionized nebula in a low-metallicity galaxy. These JWST observations of Ho~II~X--1 show that an accreting black hole in a low-metallicity galaxy is responsible for the extreme ionization of the surrounding nebula on ${\sim}100$\,pc scales.

title: CHARIZARD: A High-throughput Generic Pipeline for Present and Upcoming Interferometers
comment: Submitted to The Open Journal of Astrophysics
summary: Radio interferometers now deliver wide bandwidths and high sensitivity, and with them data volumes that are awkward to reduce by hand and slow to reduce automatically. The limit is not always the algorithms themselves but the way the work is laid out across the computing available. We present CHARIZARD, a pipeline that carries a raw measurement set through flagging, cross-calibration, self-calibration and imaging to full-Stokes images, and which is built around distributing that work. The observing band is repartitioned into sub-bands that stay independent through cross-calibration, the unit of work becomes the target field and sub-band pair at self-calibration, and stages touching disjoint data are run together. Each stage is an ordinary PBS or SLURM job, submitted and tracked by a scheduler-agnostic layer, and every computation runs inside a single rootless container, so a user holding no administrative rights gets the same behaviour on any cluster. We benchmark the pipeline on MeerKAT measurements with full polarization calibration. Residual on-axis instrumental polarization is $0.13$ per cent in linear and $0.06$ per cent in circular; the deepest field reaches $4.11\,μ$Jy~beam$^{-1}$ over $787$~MHz with $σ_I/σ_V = 1.010$; positions agree with RACS-low to better than $0.4\arcsec$ and flux densities to a median ratio of $1.06$. A $1.5$~TB track completes $48.6$ core-hours of work in $18.4$~hours with self-calibration and polarization calibration. The next generation of the radio telescopes will not be short of data. CHARIZARD attempts to show how the distribution of the work provides a useful alternative for handling the staggering processing requirements.

title: Two-variable longitudinal distribution of the $Λ_b$ in a three-quark light-front model
summary: We determine a normalized two-variable longitudinal distribution of the $Λ_b=(ud)b$ baryon from a covariant three-quark light-front wave function. The scalar $ud$ channel is selected with the good-component structure $Cγ_5γ^+$, and the two independent transverse momenta are integrated without introducing an elementary diquark. The resulting model-scale valence distribution, $Ψ_2^{\rm LF}(x_u,x_d)$, retains both the heavy--light and internal-light momentum scales of the parent wave function. It is symmetric under $x_u\leftrightarrow x_d$, is concentrated where both light-quark fractions are small, and separates the total light-pair momentum from its internal sharing. For the central parameter set we find $\langle x_u\rangle=\langle x_d\rangle=0.130$, $\langle x_b\rangle=0.739$, $\langleζ^2\rangle=0.153$, and $\langleζ^4\rangle=0.055$, where $ζ=(x_u-x_d)/(x_u+x_d)$. Parameter variations give $\langle x_u\rangle=0.130^{+0.007}_{-0.007}$, $\langle x_b\rangle=0.739^{+0.014}_{-0.014}$, $\langleζ^2\rangle=0.153^{+0.014}_{-0.016}$, and $\langleζ^4\rangle=0.055^{+0.009}_{-0.009}$. The heavy--light momentum partition is controlled mainly by $β_{b,ud}$ and $m_b$, whereas the internal $u$--$d$ sharing is most sensitive to $β_{ud}$. The result provides a compact finite-mass benchmark for three-quark longitudinal structure, with distinct observables for heavy--light momentum sharing and correlations inside the light pair.

title: Leptogenesis with a GeV-Scale Quasi-Dirac Neutrino
comment: 14 pages, 10 figures, and 1 table. Comments are welcome
summary: We discuss leptogenesis in a model with a GeV-scale quasi-Dirac neutral lepton, comprising mainly sterile states, which is accessible to future experiments. In particular, we show that Higgs-decay leptogenesis can naturally arise from the type-I seesaw mechanism with spontaneously broken global lepton number together with a discrete $Z_2$ symmetry, yielding two quasi-degenerate right-handed neutrinos (RHNs) which, to excellent approximation, form a single Dirac neutrino, with a tiny mass splitting as required for resonant enhancement generated by higher-dimensional lepton-number-violating operators. Incorporating finite-temperature effects, we show that the observed baryon asymmetry can be successfully generated through thermal Higgs decays for 0.1-10 GeV mass quasi-Dirac neutrinos, with the CP asymmetry arising from the interplay between the vacuum and thermal contributions to the mass splitting. In the parameter region of successful leptogenesis, the quasi-Dirac neutrino is accessible to future heavy neutral lepton searches at SHiP, MATHUSLA and FCC-ee. In addition, the same symmetry-breaking sector gives rise to unstable domain walls whose annihilation can generate a stochastic gravitational-wave background, providing a complementary probe of the framework.

title: Stability and dynamics of bumblebee models
summary: In this work, we study vector field theories with spontaneous Lorentz violation induced by a nonderivative potential $V(X)$ (with $X = B_μB^μ$), known as bumblebee models, with a Maxwell kinetic term in Minkowski spacetime. We confirm a recent result showing that a class of smooth potentials, including a purely cubic potential, leads to a Hamiltonian density that is bounded from below and assumes a global minimum for nonzero timelike expectation values of the vector field satisfying $X = b^2 > 0$, inducing spontaneous Lorentz-symmetry breaking. We show explicitly that the standard quadratic potential has a Hamiltonian that is unbounded from below and thus unstable. We analyze the Hamiltonian equations of motion for the timelike case and demonstrate that they are regular at the global minimum. Furthermore, we examine the linearized spectrum of small fluctuations around the minimum. We also study particular solutions with spherical symmetry analytically and numerically, without assuming linearization. We find that the time evolution of smooth initial configurations can develop shock-like singularities, and we explain why this behavior is expected in this model. We also identify a subset of the space of field configurations in which the field equations cease to be hyperbolic, leading to a breakdown of well-posedness of the Cauchy initial-value problem.

title: From Accelerating Rotating Black Holes to a Swirling Universe
summary: We demonstrate that the swirling universe can be recovered through a coordinated horizon-degeneration and scaling procedure applied to the Kerr C-metric. The construction exploits the horizon structure of accelerating, rotating black holes, which allows their inner and outer horizons to coalesce while simultaneously approaching the acceleration horizon. By magnifying the near-acceleration-horizon region faster than the black hole horizons approach it, the pair of accelerating, rotating black holes is pushed to an infinite proper distance, while a finite gravitomagnetic twist survives. The resulting geometry reproduces precisely the swirling universe, providing a physical interpretation of its intrinsic rotation as the gravitational remnant of rotating black holes sent to infinity.

title: ACACIAS II: element abundances for 39 stars in the dwarf galaxy Sculptor
summary: Element abundances in nearby galaxies provide insights into their chemical enrichment histories and place the Milky Way and its neighbours in a broader cosmological context. These systems can be studied through individual stars, whose resolved spectra enable the construction of a chemical abundance census of the Local Group. We present the second stage of the ACACIAS (extra-galactic ArChAeology with Cannon Inferred Abundances from resolved integral field unit Spectra) program, which aims to build the first homogeneous data set of stellar abundances across dwarf galaxies spanning a range of masses for comparison with Milky Way properties. We analyse low-resolution (R=1800), low-SNR (signal-to-noise ratio, ~ 25) MUSE spectra for 39 stars in the Sculptor dwarf spheroidal galaxy. Using the data-driven method The Cannon, we combine high-fidelity labels from the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) survey with MUSE-like Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) spectra to analyse the MUSE data. This enables the determination of [Mg/Fe], [Mn/Fe], [C/Fe], [N/Fe], and [Al/Fe] on the APOGEE abundance scale, with precisions of σ = 0.09-0.37 dex. Comparing model configurations, we show that [Mg/Fe], [Mn/Fe], and [C/Fe] are best recovered from targeted spectral windows, whereas stellar parameters and [Al/Fe] benefit from full-spectrum information with telluric masking. This reflects the complementary strengths of restricted-window models, which recover abundances from direct spectral features, and full-spectrum models, which exploit correlations with other labels when diagnostic features are weak or absent. Our approach demonstrates the potential of low-resolution, low-SNR stellar spectra to build homogeneous datasets for extragalactic archaeology to better understand the chemical enrichment diversity of the Local Group.

title: The Birth and Early Feedback of Massive Star Clusters Across the Local Universe
comment: Part of the ALMA2040 White Paper Series
summary: Young massive star clusters (YMCs; ${\gtrsim}10^4\rm\,M_\odot$) represent a distinct, extreme mode of star formation and the closest present-day analogues of the environments in which globular clusters and Cosmic Noon stellar populations assembled. Given the extreme dust extinction in the earliest phase of YMC formation, (sub-)millimeter observations are the only means of probing their assembly and early feedback. Pioneering works with ALMA are limited to individual region studies and to the most massive YMCs in them, leaving many open questions about the initial conditions of YMC formation, the integrated star and cluster formation efficiencies, the dominant pre-supernova feedback channels, and the prevalence and reach of cluster-driven outflows. ALMA2040 will enable mass-complete, resolved surveys in hundreds of host galaxies, transforming the study of massive cluster formation and feedback from individual case analyses into statistical measurements across the full range of galactic environments.

title: Nonleptonic decays of the double-charmed baryon $Ξ_{cc}^{+}$ with dynamically determined baryon wave functions
summary: Motivated by the recent observation of the double-charmed baryon $Ξ_{cc}^{+}$ by the LHCb Collaboration, we systematically investigate the two-body nonleptonic decays of the $Ξ_{cc}^{+}$ into a single-charmed baryon and a light pseudoscalar meson. In our calculation, both factorizable and nonfactorizable decay amplitudes are evaluated within the framework of nonrelativistic quark model combined with the baryon wave functions dynamically determined by numerically solving the three-body Schrödinger equation with a nonrelativistic potential model. In particular, the nonfactorizable $W$-exchange amplitudes are estimated under pole model by considering $J^{P}=1/2^{\pm}$ low-lying intermediate charmed-baryon poles, and our results show that these contributions are comparable to or even dominate the factorizable amplitudes in several decay channels. Moreover, assuming a lifetime of $τ_{Ξ_{cc}^{+}}=47~\text{fs}$, we predict relatively large branching fractions for several CF decays, including $\mathcal{B}(Ξ_{cc}^{+}\toΞ_{c}^{\prime0}π^{+})=8.90\%$, $\mathcal{B}(Ξ_{cc}^{+}\toΩ_{c}^{0}K^{+})=7.09\%$, $\mathcal{B}(Ξ_{cc}^{+}\toΣ_{c}^{+}\bar{K}^{0})=6.92\%$, $\mathcal{B}(Ξ_{cc}^{+}\toΞ_{c}^{+}π^{0})=5.28\%$, and $\mathcal{B}(Ξ_{cc}^{+}\toΣ_{c}^{++}K^{-})=5.17\%$. These channels are promising candidates for future experimental searches at the LHCb.

title: Self Calibrated Galaxy Groups from the DESI DR1 Bright Galaxy Survey
comment: 32 pages, 26 Figures, submitted to ApJ. See https://ianw89.github.io/catalogs.html or https://data.desi.lbl.gov/doc/releases/dr1/#value-added-catalogs to acquire the catalog

We find these non-parametric HODs can be fit by standard HOD models, with satellite power-law index $α$ values around 0.75 for star-forming galaxies and around 1.1 for quiescent objects. In agreement with recent results, we find that the quenched fraction of central galaxies depends mostly on halo mass and is nearly independent of central galaxy stellar mass for galaxies more massive than $10^{10.3}$ $M_\odot h^{-1}$ and halos more massive than $10^{12.2}$ $M_\odot h^{-1}$.
